target_customer: Websites and enterprises facing bots, credential stuffing and automated attacks
problem: Automated attacks and credential abuse were hard to separate from real users without hurting user experience.

founders.name: Sreenath Kurupati
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page without background.

founders.name: Sridhar Machiroutu
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder in coverage of the Akamai deal.

technical_complexity.rationale: Real-time machine learning detection of bots that hide from users needed behavioral modeling and a low-latency pipeline.

defensibility.rationale: Detection models improve with traffic data, but well-funded rivals and CDN vendors could build similar capabilities.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Akamai bought CyberFend for an undisclosed all-cash sum announced December 2016 to strengthen Bot Manager.

market_need_then: Credential abuse and scraping were rising enterprise concerns, and Akamai itself launched Bot Manager in 2016 and sought the technology.

brand_strength.rationale: No brand coverage found. The product was referred to as BotFender in a 2016 Finovate interview, suggesting inconsistent naming.

outcome_analysis: CyberFend built machine learning bot detection, joined YC in Winter 2015, and was acquired by Akamai in December 2016 for an undisclosed all-cash amount that Akamai called immaterial. The deal fit Akamai's push to extend Bot Manager against credential abuse. With about 3 million dollars reported raised, it looks like a small technology exit.
notes: cyberfend.com did not resolve (dead or blocked), not worked around. Investors YC, SV Angel and A Capital come from the YC page and Akamai coverage but no round amounts or dates were found; Village.ai reports 3M total, unverified so no rounds recorded. Dated competitor search returned only current profiles of Distil, Shape and PerimeterX, so the list is empty. Akamai release dated 2016-12-18 or 12-19 depending on outlet.
